assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.1 [2781,2968) identifies the work notice as the source of the passages. [5354,6310) supplies the printed-copy threshold, corresponding covers and ordered overflow guidance. The broader media wording appears in the later editions.

challenge.method: Tested 100 and 101 printed copies, a notice requiring no Cover Texts, and 101 nonprinted copies on media commonly sold with printed covers. Compared the adjacent Opaque-copy paragraph.
challenge.results: Exactly 100 misses the threshold. At 101 printed copies the cover rule applies if the notice requires texts. A notice requiring none leaves that condition unsatisfied. Customary printed packaging alone does not bring nonprinted copies within the 1.1 wording. Independently, publishing or distributing 101 Opaque copies triggers a Transparent copy with each or a public network location stated in or with each, regardless of Cover Texts.

limitations: The same paragraph also requires legible publisher identification on both covers and the full title on the front with every word equally prominent and visible. The claim addresses text placement only.
reasoning: GNU 1.1 §§1 and 3 tie the cover duty to publication of more than 100 printed copies and to the work’s notice requiring designated passages. The publisher must display them legibly on their respective covers. For overflow, §3 says the publisher should place as many of the first listed passages as reasonably fit on the cover and continue the remainder on adjacent pages.
